html:
The Wangkumara are an Aboriginal people of southwest Queensland, in channel country along the Wilson and Bulloo rivers and around Thargomindah, near the border with New South Wales.

This is a land of floods and droughts, where rivers spread into wide channels after rain and shrink to waterholes. Neighbours on the map include the Yawarawarka and Yandruwandha to the west and the Karenggapa to the south. Seed grinding and fishing in the waterholes were important.

Pastoralists moved into the region in the 1860s and 1870s, after the Burke and Wills expedition crossed the area nearby. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Wangkumara are an Aboriginal people of southwest Queensland, in channel country along the Wilson and Bulloo rivers and around Thargomindah, near the border with New South Wales.
